Andy Tulloch reached the semi-finals of the 110m hurdles, Chris Rawlinson took part in the 400m hurdles, Sean Baldock was one of the team in the heats of the 4x400m relay and Nick Sweeney threw the discus for Ireland.
Discus ~ Nick Sweeney A repeat of his 64.28m set in Helsingborg, Sweden, in July would not only have seen Nick through the qualifying round, it would have taken him to 5th place in the final.
Above: Tremendous discus throwing came from Nick Sweeney throughout the summer of '98 and Helsinborg, Sweden, almost became a second home to the 30 year-old Irishman.

In the throws we welcomed another newcomer Nick Sweeney. Nick couldn't compete for us last year due to an operation but proved his value by winning the 'A' discus and finishing second in the 'A' shot for big points score (30).
The discus was a 1,2 with Nick Sweeney well ahead of Newham's Paul Head. The 100m turned out to be historic due to the unexpected return of Linford Christie.
